verification_report.summary:
The complete supplied proof passes sequential verification under the expressly accepted inputs and the validated scopes of the completed prerequisite reports. Eighteen statement checks and five reference checks found no critical errors or gaps. Both positive-exponent existence and uniqueness, and zero-exponent existence with uniqueness of the positive scalar, are established. The book was read without modification.

All requested prerequisite reports are complete. common_barrier_compactness_01 has overall verdict wrong solely because a standalone monotone-sequence remark omits the requirement that a decreasing limit be genuine. Its report expressly validates the fixed-measure exponential lemma, common-barrier criterion and dominated-continuity corollary used here. Their actual monotone sequences have explicit genuine lower barriers. Thus that unrelated error does not invalidate these applications. weighted_measure_addition_01 and bounded_subsolution_01 have verdict correct; their earlier pending conditions are resolved within these validated prerequisite scopes. The classical local convergence input remains expressly accepted rather than independently reproved in this audit.

In part (1), the supersolution supplies a nonempty family of finite weighted measures, with masses bounded by mu(X). Exponential order applied to (w,u_j) gives u_j<=w. The scaled background (1-epsilon)theta is semipositive and big, so the bounded auxiliary equation is available. The positive current splitting for h=psi+phi_epsilon gives the stated weighted lower bound on common finite levels and then globally off negligible poles. Although h may be more singular than phi, h preceq u_j is exactly the required order. Each u_j has a genuine smaller-background competitor obtained by translating phi_epsilon. Exponential order applied to (u_j,h) therefore gives u_j>=h and uniform finite bounds for M_j.

The relative estimate is correctly applied to v_j=u_j-M_j, with supremum zero and the fixed density bound exp(lambda sup w)f. Combining its bounds with those for M_j produces a uniform strip around phi. This prevents L1 collapse and meets every hypothesis of common-barrier dominated continuity with a fixed finite non-pluripolar dominating measure. The canonical limit has ordinary type phi, and capacity and raw weak convergence follow.

The weighted weak-limit argument is valid. Domination by mu preserves nu0<=nu<=mu. Fixed-measure exponential convergence controls changing exp(lambda u_j) to exp(lambda u) in L1(mu). Approximating the latter fixed weight by continuous functions in L1(mu) controls both the approximating and limiting measures uniformly, so only legitimate continuous weak tests are used. The raw and weighted limits identify MAext(u)=exp(lambda u)nu. Cancellation is performed where u is finite; its pole set is mu-null. Testing with the constant one gives nu(X)=B, so the maximum is attained. Radon-Nikodym yields 0<=g<=f, hence g belongs to Lp.

A nonzero residual f-g remains nonnegative, nonzero and Lp, so its supersolution exists. Its weighted measure has strictly positive mass: otherwise its raw measure vanishes, and strict domination for (v,v+1) with coefficient zero contradicts genuineness. The addition theorem applies to the actual pair u,v in the same ordinary type; their weighted sum is finite and bounded by mu. The resulting potential is admissible and has mass strictly greater than B. This excludes the residual. Positive-exponent uniqueness follows by exponential order in both directions.

In part (2), the displayed H_j has weighted measure exp(-(h+||h||infinity)/j)f dV<=f dV. Constants provide genuine smaller-background competitors for bounded H_j, and u_j preceq H_j. Thus exponential order with first potential H_j gives u_j<=H_j, yielding the stated uniform upper bound for c_j. Normalization then gives MAext(v_j)<=C f dV, so the relative estimate again supplies fixed barriers and the common-barrier corollary gives the required limiting ordinary type and raw weak convergence.

For q=p/(p-1), uniform exponential integrability bounds ||v_j||Lq. The inequality 0<=1-exp(v_j/j)<=|v_j|/j and Holder give an O(1/j) error in L1(f dV). Bounded c_j converging to c therefore gives total variation convergence of the right sides to c f dV, identifying the limiting equation. The limit retains a genuine smaller-background envelope; zero-measure domination excludes c=0. For unequal positive scalars, strict domination applies to (a,b+t) with coefficient c_a/c_b<1 for every t. A common finite point rules out arbitrarily large translations. This proves scalar uniqueness only; no equality-case potential uniqueness is inferred.

The required arXiv theorem searches returned unrelated statements. Fallback primary-source verification confirmed the model definition, ordinary-type scope and respective uniqueness claims in [ALS26 v1, Definition 2.13 and Theorems 5.4 and 5.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02339v1). Replacing omega^n by a smooth positive dV preserves the Lp hypothesis through a bounded positive density factor. These source theorems were used for comparison only. Every problem hypothesis has a justified role, and neither proof imports BMP, PVP, a uniform positive lower mass, or an unsupported closure assertion for a larger relative class.
